stem: A multiplayer game studio's network team runs a UDP-based matchmaking service and needs static IP addresses with fast failover to the healthiest regional endpoint; the traffic cannot be cached.

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront, configured to cache the matchmaking traffic at edge locations
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing alone, relying on DNS TTL expiry for failover
AWS Global Accelerator, using static anycast IP addresses and health-based routing to the healthiest endpoint
An API Gateway stage cache placed in front of the matchmaking service

rationale: AWS Global Accelerator uses static anycast IP addresses and the AWS global network to route TCP/UDP traffic, including non-cacheable and non-HTTP workloads, to the healthiest endpoint, which is exactly what this UDP matchmaking service needs. CloudFront caches HTTP(S) content at the edge; it has no role for non-cacheable UDP traffic. Route 53 latency-based routing on its own depends on clients honoring DNS TTLs, so failover is only as fast as those TTLs expire and re-resolve, which is slower than Global Accelerator's health-based routing over static IPs. An API Gateway stage cache only caches HTTP API responses for a stage; it has nothing to do with routing raw UDP traffic to a healthy endpoint.
